reasoning_traces.think:
VPD operates under the principle of distilling semantic structure from noisy teacher poses into a student network trained on unlabeled sport video. The core innovation lies in using temporal derivatives Δp_t to encode motion dynamics, which enables robust action recognition even when raw pose estimation fails due to motion blur or occlusion. The method assumes that while individual pose estimates may be unreliable, their temporal evolution carries discriminative signal. This is formalized through a dual objective: minimizing reconstruction error of both pose and its derivative. The teacher network (HRNet or VIPE*) provides weak supervision without requiring labeled data, enabling few-shot learning in domains with sparse annotations. The student network learns to extract compact, view-invariant descriptors that generalize well across unseen actions. In GSI, these descriptors enable probabilistic action classification with calibrated uncertainty bounds. In GSE, they support dynamic state transitions and temporal reasoning for athlete behavior prediction.
